tells.tell: Faceted low-poly planes and visible shading kinks on the curved chassis surfaces; edges are sharp-hard with no consistent moulded/machined radius, flat facets read as polygons
Uniform flat olive paint with a faint procedural mottle; no handling wear, scuffs, dust, edge rub-through or fingerprints on the most-touched surface of the rifle
Bolt body is a perfect chrome mirror stripe with no machining marks, jeweling, oil film or carbon; shroud/handle are untextured matte black plastic-looking
Knob is a perfect smooth sphere on a plain cylinder stem; real knobs have knurling/texture or a tapered transition
Scope anodizing is spotless and uniform, no lettering, serials or knurl texture on the ocular ring; matte finish shows no micro variation
Out-of-focus areas carry fine grainy path-tracer noise instead of smooth optical bokeh; the defocus falls off too evenly for a real macro lens at 35 cm
Featureless seamless grey gradient with no studio sweep texture; lighting is soft and directionless, typical of an HDRI/area-light Blender studio
No reticle, no sight picture, no exit pupil image: the ocular is just a black disc with a single round blob highlight; a real eyepiece at eye relief shows the magnified scene and crosshair
The highlight is a perfect uniform grey circle with noisy interior, a reflection of a disc area light, with no lens-coating tint (green/magenta) or multiple element reflections
Heavy monochromatic sampling noise across flat regions and inside the blur, unlike sensor noise (no chroma, no pattern), plus a hard horizontal grey band background reading as a CG wall/floor seam
Eyepiece reads as a perfect circle with no rubber eyecup ridge or diopter ring visible even in defocus
Two blown-out elliptical light pools on the floor and a dark vignette dome: classic Blender spot/area lights on an infinite plane; no real studio sweep produces this pattern
Contact shadow under the rifle is blocky/stepped with rectangular staircase artifacts (shadow/AO or reflection resolution artifacts) and a ghost reflection band offset from the rifle
Rifle looks like it floats: weak grounding, bipod feet and buttpad lack crisp contact occlusion
Flat uniform olive with no variation at this distance; the scope and barrel are identical toy-like black
Barrel is a long perfect cylinder with plain flutes and a simple can-like muzzle device, no crown detail
Stepped/notched irregular ridge along the forend top edge and visible facet kinks on the side bevels; the vent slots are simple extruded stadiums with soft uniform bevels
Olive coating has a uniform fine procedural noise but zero wear on edges, around the mag well or bolt handle path; reads as clean CG paint
Grip texture is a bump-only noise stipple that looks pasted on; it does not wrap or terminate at panel borders like a moulded texture would
Dial numerals are tiny and soft, no other markings anywhere (no brand, serial, magnification numbers on the zoom ring), unnaturally sterile
Objective shows a single clean crescent highlight and pure black interior, no coating tint or reflection of the room/camera
Magazine is a plain box with two engraved lines and simple bevel, no follower window or baseplate detail; joins to the stock with a hard intersection
Blocky stepped shadow artifacts on the floor at lower left; uniform soft grey sweep with no texture
Hard horizontal seam where a darker grey wall meets the floor, an untextured CG cyclorama with no cove
Stepped blocky shadow shapes under the buttstock on the floor (left), a render artifact no photograph would show
Leg extensions are bright ribbed chrome with perfect regular rings; inner legs are clean with no oxidation; feet are perfectly smooth rubber cylinders
Feet show weak contact shadow and no compression into the floor, rifle looks weightless
Buttstock is boxy with flat slab cheek riser and plain round dots for adjusters; transitions between blocks are hard boolean-like joins
Paint tone is lighter and cleaner than in other views, uniform with no edge wear or dirt
Barrel runs out of frame with even smooth reflection gradient, no micro-scratches or dust picked up by the key light

overall: All five images are CG; none would pass as a product photograph. The strongest give-aways are render_rig: the Blender-style studio (two blown elliptical light pools and dark dome in tp_3m, hard wall/floor seam in deployed_34 and ads_eyepiece), stepped blocky shadow artifacts on the floor in tp_3m, hero_34 and deployed_34, monochrome path-tracer noise in defocused areas, and an eyepiece with no reticle or sight picture in ads_eyepiece. Material tells are next: perfectly clean uniform olive paint with no edge wear, a mirror-chrome bolt with no machining marks, sterile scope with almost no markings, and bump-only grip stipple. Geometry tells are secondary but visible at close range: faceted shading kinks and a notched irregular ridge on the forend/chassis, boxy boolean-joined buttstock, plain sphere bolt knob and simple box magazine. Fix the rig (proper cove backdrop, shadow resolution, denoise/more samples, real scope optics) first, then add wear and markings.
